newsitem.title: INDIA: Israeli president to pay nostalgic visit to India.
newsitem.headline: Israeli president to pay nostalgic visit to India.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman will begin an emotional visit to India this month, his first since he served as a British pilot here 50 years ago, Israeli officials said on Thursday.
"The president will be mixing the highest level of contacts between the two countries with a nostalgic tour of the country where he served as a pilot in 1946," an Israeli official told Reuters.

Weizman begins his six-day state visit on December 29 in New Delhi, where he will celebrate the new year with a reception. He will then travel to the southern city of Bangalore to visit his former British air base there.
"Weizman's military career began when he joined Great Britain's Royal Air Force during World War II, serving in Egypt and India," an Israeli Embassy statement said.
Later, as head of the Israeli Air Force, "he was the architect of Israel's decisive victory over Egypt's air force during the 1967 Six-Day War", the statement said.
Traditionally pro-Arab India established diplomatic ties with Israel in January 1992, days after Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat endorsed the move during a visit to New Delhi.

Weizman will be the guest of India's President Shankar Dayal Sharma, whose highest-level contact with any Israeli leader so far has been a meeting in New Delhi with then-foreign minister Shimon Peres in 1993.
Israeli officials said they were working out the details of at least three agreements on cultural ties, trade and commerce expected to be signed during Weizman's visit.
Senior Israeli industrialists acompanying Weizman will hold talks with their Indian counterparts in New Delhi and Bombay, the last leg of the visit, officials said.
India, which has a small but dwindling Jewish population, does not recognise Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
Indian officials turned down a proposed visit by the Jerusalem Symphony Orchestra over fears its name would annoy Indian Moslems and New Delhi's Arab friends.
"With our closer cultural ties expected from the visit, we hope such misunderstandings will be removed," said a former Indian civil servant, a Jew.
